claims.author: sedited
claims.quote: Maybe it would be preferable to push forward #30342 before this is done?
claims.request: Push forward #30342 before changing the logging API

status_by.quote: On the question of whether to push forward with this PR or #30342 first: I think this PR should have much higher priority than #30342.

claims.status_note: author argued this PR should take priority because it changes the API incompatibly while #30342 is backwards compatible

claims.author: stringintech
claims.harm: Accepting per-connection handles on logging configuration functions suggests per-connection isolation while calling them still overrides settings globally across all connections
claims.quote: keep the API consistent with what it's currently capable of

status_by.quote: My preference was to wait for #30342

claims.status_note: stringintech reiterated preference to wait for #30342 after author's reply

claims.author: stringintech
claims.question: Whether delaying StartLogging() to context creation means context-free operations miss logs and whether it would need to move back if such operations log in the future
claims.quote: This delay could mean logs won't be produced by context-free operations (like btck_script_pubkey_verify())

status_by.quote: I am a little surprised there would be any context-free operations except very basic ones that shouldn't log

claims.status_note: author replied that non-trivial operations producing logs should have an associated context object

claims.author: stickies-v
claims.harm: Exposing a new public interface before internal logging refactorings like #30342 proceed risks unexpected behavior and misses insights that internal changes could provide for interface design
claims.quote: internal logging refactorings / changes (e.g. #30342, but also others) may surface roadblocks or ideas that inform us about a better interface design, so waiting a bit more seems helpful to me
claims.status_note: stickies-v pushed back with an Approach NACK, arguing interface and functional changes should happen atomically in #30342

claims.author: stickies-v
claims.harm: If context does not own the logging connection, object lifetime management becomes brittle and destroying a logging connection could leave the associated context in an invalid state
claims.quote: managing lifetimes becomes more brittle, i.e. users must ensure `logger` is kept alive for the duration of `context`

status_by.quote: I agree then that there is no need for context to own the logging connection.

claims.status_note: stickies-v agreed that context does not need to own the logging connection
